verdict.rationale: Semgrep's open-source scanning engine installs and runs entirely locally: `semgrep scan` needs no account or login, and by default code is never uploaded. That is self-hosting of the core analysis engine. However, triage, CI findings aggregation, Managed Scans and the API all live in the hosted Semgrep AppSec Platform, and a community user notes Supply Chain is not open source and may require uploading code. missing for 10: a documented self-hosted or on-prem deployment of the AppSec Platform (findings triage/dashboard), offline operation of paid products like Supply Chain/Secrets, independent hands-on corroboration of fully air-gapped use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Semgrep analyzes code locally on your computer or in your build environment: by default, code is never upload
semgrep scan - This is the recommended command for scanning local codebases or scanning a project when you don't have a Semgrep account
You do **not** need to be logged in to run a scan.
You can run local Semgrep CLI scans with the Semgrep command-line tool.
